title: Bank Marketing · UCI
description: Who should be contacted when the team cannot call everyone? An exercise using actual telephone campaigns from a Portuguese bank.

dataset.name: Bank Marketing · UCI

provenance.authors: Moro, S., Rita, P., & Cortez, P. (2014)

transformations: bank.csv extracted unchanged from bank.zip in the official archive.
pdays = -1 encoded as a never-contacted indicator in prepare_bank.py.

facts.label: Observation unit
facts.value: A customer contacted during a telephone campaign

facts.label: Intended use
facts.value: Teaching simulation: prioritize contacts when call capacity is limited

facts.label: Repeated customers or time structure
facts.value: Cannot be verified: the extract has neither a customer identifier nor a complete date.

facts.label: Effect of calling on subscription
facts.value: Not measured by these historical observations.

variables.name: previous
variables.label: Previous contacts
variables.description: Number of contacts before this campaign.

variables.name: pdays
variables.label: Days elapsed
variables.description: Days since contact in a previous campaign.

variables.name: duration
variables.label: Call duration
variables.description: Duration of the current call, known only afterwards; used only in the leakage counterexample.

constraints: Exercise only: no decisions from the previous incident project are imported.
No new training from the companion.
limitations: Random historical extract: an exercise using real data, not a campaign recommendation.
The file also includes personal characteristics; this small model uses none of them and is not a fairness assessment.
ai_guidance: Distinguish selected contacts from observed subscriptions.
An unselected subscription is not an established lost sale: there is no evidence that calling would have caused it.

start.title: Starting point
start.objective: Discover the data, target, and provenance before modeling.
start.lead: Who should be contacted when the team cannot call everyone?

blocks.label: Tutorial guide
blocks.text: We will explore actual telephone campaigns from a Portuguese bank. The target is an observed subscription. Discover the data, compare a reference, identify leakage, and examine call capacity.

blocks.title: What does a row look like?
blocks.intro: A telephone campaign record with its observed outcome. Six training examples illustrate both responses (3 yes, 3 no); they do not represent the actual class frequency.

blocks.title: Understand features and special values
blocks.note: pdays = −1 : {{x:special.no_previous_contact}} training rows ; poutcome « unknown » : {{x:special.unknown_outcome}} training rows.

blocks.label: Keep in mind
blocks.text: Random historical bank.csv extract. An exercise using real data, not a campaign recommendation.

use.title: Use before modeling
use.objective: Specify the decision: select contacts before calling, with limited capacity.
use.lead: Decision studied: select contacts before making calls.

blocks.label: Tutorial guide
blocks.text: Target y records an observed subscription. Our scenario simulates prioritization. Actual use would require verifying when each feature is available and whether calling changes the decision.

blocks.question: What should be clarified before selecting a model?

options.label: Call capacity and the decision made before each call
options.feedback: Yes. We are exploring contact prioritization. Available call capacity determines the trade-off to examine.

options.label: The algorithm with the highest score
options.feedback: A score defines neither team capacity nor selection utility. Start with the intended use.

blocks.summary: Predicting a subscription does not measure the effect of calling
blocks.text: The data describes past campaigns. It does not establish that a subscription would have been lost without a call. We therefore discuss retrieved or unselected observed subscriptions, not established sales gained or lost.

baseline.title: The accuracy trap
baseline.objective: Compare the model with a constant reference to recognize a misleading score.
baseline.lead: A simple reference helps identify a misleading score.

blocks.note: The reference achieves {{r:model-reference.accuracy}} accuracy without retrieving any subscription. Results use {{p:stratified-70-30.validation}} held-out rows and threshold 0.50.

options.label: No: examine retrieved subscriptions and call workload
options.feedback: Correct. Always predicting no can look effective while retrieving no subscriptions.

options.label: Yes: most predictions are correct
options.feedback: The reference selects no contacts. Its accuracy mainly reflects the frequency of non-subscriptions.

blocks.text: Accuracy: share of correct predictions. Recall: share of observed subscriptions retrieved. AUC: ranking quality between subscriptions and non-subscriptions. No single metric measures commercial benefit.

leakage.title: Identify leakage
leakage.objective: Understand why call duration cannot decide whom to call.
leakage.lead: Call duration can help predict the outcome… after the call.

results.label: With duration · unavailable before the call

blocks.note: duration is the actual duration of the corresponding call in seconds. This column is not fabricated. Adding it deliberately creates a counterexample for our pre-call decision.

blocks.question: Can call duration be used to decide whom to call?

options.label: No: it is known after the call
options.feedback: Correct. duration is a real column, but it is unavailable before the call. A higher score does not make the feature usable.

options.label: Yes: it improves the ranking
options.feedback: The score uses information from the future relative to the decision. A train/validation split does not fix that.

blocks.label: Tutorial guide
blocks.text: Exclude duration from the model used to select contacts. Leakage need not produce perfect accuracy to invalidate an operational comparison.

protocol.title: A fair comparison
protocol.objective: Read the exploratory protocol and its limits: random splitting does not establish future-campaign performance.
protocol.lead: A reproducible comparison with visible limitations.

blocks.label: The exploratory protocol
blocks.text: {{p:stratified-70-30.train}} training rows and {{p:stratified-70-30.validation}} validation rows, stratified 70/30 split, seed {{g:seed}}. Standardization and category encoding are fitted on training data only. bank.csv is a random subset of historical campaigns: without complete dates or customer identifiers, customer independence and future-campaign performance cannot be assessed. Two regressions were fitted to prepare this exercise; displayed results are precomputed and reused.

blocks.question: Does this random split establish quality on the next campaign?

options.label: No: temporal evaluation and repeated-customer checks are needed
options.feedback: Correct. This extract has no complete date or customer identifier. The tutorial supports comparisons, not a generalization claim about the next campaign.

options.label: Yes: two partitions are enough
options.feedback: A random mixture of historical campaigns does not necessarily represent the future. Customer independence cannot be checked here.

selection.title: From score to action
selection.objective: Choose a selection threshold: how many contacts to select and which observed subscriptions to retrieve.
selection.lead: How many contacts should be selected, and which subscriptions are retrieved?

blocks.label: Contact selection threshold
blocks.hint: Existing preview; apply the choice to attach this result. No new training.

blocks.label: Tutorial guide
blocks.text: Compare two thresholds: which better fits team capacity? Counts describe past observations. They predict neither sales caused by calls nor future-campaign performance.
Choosing a threshold on this validation already uses its results. A protocol suited to time and customers would then be needed to evaluate the retained selection.

constraints.title: Your constraints
constraints.objective: Express the constraints that make a result usable.
constraints.lead: Express the constraints that make a result usable.

blocks.question: Which teaching constraint would you like to explore?

options.label: No additional constraint
options.feedback: Keep a simple logistic regression as the starting point without treating it as a business requirement.

options.label: A model that is simple to explain
options.feedback: Logistic regression helps examine relationships between features and scores. Its coefficients do not establish causality.

blocks.label: In this demo
blocks.text: Call duration cannot select contacts before a call. The initial model is deliberately small. Real use would also require checking data availability, the population, contact rules, and selection fairness.

handoff.title: Review and hand over
handoff.objective: Connect exercise choices to exploratory results and limitations.
handoff.lead: You have connected actual data to a concrete decision.

blocks.label: Tutorial guide
blocks.text: We distinguished a flattering reference, a feature unavailable before the decision, and a selection trade-off. Your choice belongs to this Bank Marketing exercise and imports no decision into the previous incident project.

blocks.title: Your handoff

blocks.text: Buttons start no campaign, training, or final validation.
